paragraphs: One-line judgment: audiologists are not about "testing hearing and fitting a hearing aid", but about closing history and chief complaint, ear canal and eardrum examination, audiological testing (pure-tone audiometry, speech audiometry, acoustic immittance, auditory evoked potentials, and so on), differential diagnosis, intervention plans (hearing aids, cochlear implants, auditory training, and communication guidance), outcome verification, and follow-up records into a traceable clinical chain; people who just want a quick sale and are unwilling to verify test conditions and records item by item are not suited to it.

Signals to keep exploring: you can verify equipment status and transducer matching according to protocol and check test conditions and masking, distinguish conductive from sensorineural hearing loss and write clearly the differential points and referral indications, are willing to keep recording test results and outcome verification, and stop and escalate when the diagnosis is unclear, medical devices are involved, or the practice authorization is exceeded.

Conditions to pause investment first: you have not yet completed a full intake, testing, and result recording process under any supervised conditions, or you can only explain your interest by "liking to help people with hearing loss"; also, do not treat course grades, one volunteer service placement, or knowing one fitting software program as proof that you can independently issue audiological conclusions, write hearing aid prescriptions, or take on diagnostic and treatment responsibility. Diagnosis, prescriptions, cochlear implant programming, and hearing aid fitting must be carried out by personnel with the corresponding qualifications and authorization according to regulations, and this page does not provide diagnostic, prescription, or programming instructions.

Education and authority must be verified separately: O*NET lists 29-1181.00 as Job Zone Five (SVP 8.0 and above), and among respondents 95% believe a doctorate is required and 5% believe postdoctoral training is required; the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook lists a doctorate or professional degree (Au.D.) as the typical entry-level education and notes that all U.S. states require audiologists to be licensed to practice. Coursework, clinical internships, internal institutional qualification, practice licensure in the relevant jurisdiction, hearing aid fitting qualifications and medical device business requirements, and prescription and referral authority are different statuses, and must be verified item by item according to employer, position, and location; this page does not provide diagnostic, prescription, or programming instructions.

One line: this is a clinical occupation centered on assessing and intervening in hearing and related disorders, and competence depends on carrying out testing protocols, interpreting results, differential and referral judgments, intervention plans and outcome verification, and holding the practice licensure and record boundaries, rather than an interest in equipment or proficiency with a single software program.

The clinical work of audiologists can be divided into three categories: assessment and testing tasks (taking history and chief complaint, examining the ear canal and eardrum, performing pure-tone audiometry, speech audiometry, acoustic immittance, and auditory evoked potentials according to protocol, verifying test conditions and masking, interpreting results, and forming differential points); intervention and rehabilitation tasks (selecting and fitting hearing aids, programming cochlear implants, providing auditory training and communication strategy guidance, verifying outcomes, and arranging follow-up); and recording and collaboration tasks (maintaining medical records at each stage of the visit, providing advice to physicians, educational institutions, and employers, and participating in multidisciplinary teams and hearing screening programs). All three categories are premised on working within the scope of practice licensure and stopping and escalating when the diagnosis or authorization is unclear.

O*NET occupational identity and tasks: O*NET 29-1181.00 Audiologists (Bright Outlook, page updated in 2026). The official duties are to assess and treat hearing and related disorders; there are 22 official tasks, including maintaining medical records at each stage of the visit, assessing hearing and balance disorders to determine diagnosis and treatment plans, fitting, dispensing, and repairing hearing aids, administering hearing tests and examinations, monitoring patient progress, teaching communication strategies to patients, families, teachers, and employers, referring when necessary, examining and cleaning ear canals, programming and monitoring cochlear implants, conducting and supervising hearing screening programs, and measuring noise in the workplace and carrying out hearing conservation programs. Field boundaries: the task list describes group work and does not mean every position carries out all tasks. The duties do not provide operating authorization; ear canal cleaning is verified separately for state scope, institutional limits, and training. The ASHA ear canal and cerumen guidance is a professional association recommendation: limited cerumen management requires the corresponding training and supervised experience, and state licensure limits, institutional authority, and insurance must be checked. Whether an anomaly is deferred or referred follows the actual assessment and protocol, and it is not the case that any anomaly stops all activity.

China's medical device regulation is now the 2024 amendment: Article 41 provides for Class II business filing with statutory exemptions from filing, and Article 42 for Class III business licensing; the specific product classification is verified separately. Articles 48—52 require use according to the instructions, disinfection for reuse, no reuse of single-use items, and calibration and maintenance of equipment requiring it according to the instructions with records, immediate discontinuation of use and notification for repair when a safety hazard is found, and no continued use below safety standards.

Interpretation and referral | Follow the real clinical protocol | Combine the history and test records with uncertainty, and verify the actual referral division of labor; the ASHA referral guidance notes that sudden or fluctuating hearing loss requires prompt ear, nose, and throat evaluation; this page does not provide complete urgent referral procedures, and uniform retesting cannot be required in a way that delays care.

Intervention and evaluation | Follow the real position and protocol | Fitting and programming, outcome evaluation, and cochlear implant collaboration are duties; the actual personnel qualifications, specific parameters, and procedures are verified separately, and independent operation is not based on this page. The 2020 hearing aid fitter skill standard sets Level Four/intermediate worker, Level Three/advanced worker, Level Two/technician, and Level One/senior technician; Level Three includes children's play and speech audiometry, Level Two includes visual reinforcement and preschool rehabilitation, and Level One includes individualized fitting for children with special needs. This is graded assessment content and cannot be summarized as a uniform statutory threshold of a certain level for all pediatric fittings, nor does it equal physician registration or a device business qualification.

Communication and follow-up | Make adherence supportable | Teach communication strategies and auditory training to patients, families, teachers, and employers, arrange follow-up, assess adherence, and record changes in outcomes.

Records and compliance | Records are not authorization | Maintain medical records at each stage, and verify personal information permissions under the actual jurisdiction; Articles 13—14 of China's Physicians Law provide that a person who has not registered and obtained a physician practice certificate may not engage in physician practice activities, and after registration must practice according to place, category, and scope; internal institutional authorization cannot replace this. This is a rule for physician activities and does not treat all hearing testing or fitting personnel as physicians. Audiologists assess and intervene in hearing and balance disorders and are responsible for test interpretation, intervention plans, and follow-up records; hearing aid specialists focus on hearing aid selection, fitting, and after-sales service; speech-language pathologists focus on assessment and treatment of speech and language disorders; optometrists focus on visual function examination and refractive correction; occupational therapists and physical therapists focus on functional training and rehabilitation; neurologists focus on the diagnosis and treatment of nervous system diseases. Adjacent occupations share assessment and rehabilitation skills, but their objects, authorization, and responsibilities differ.
A traceable testing and intervention record

Within the scope of practice, turn the chief complaint and test results into reviewable audiological conclusions, intervention plans, and follow-up plans, and leave medical record notes explaining the test conditions, the basis for interpretation, the parameter settings, and outcome verification.
History, test results, and intervention records

The objects are the patient's hearing and balance function, ear canal and eardrum status, devices such as hearing aids and cochlear implants, and communication needs in educational and occupational settings; the basis is audiological testing protocols, device fitting and verification methods, practice licensure and institutional systems, and the applicable medical device and patient information regulations.

Not interchangeable

Degree, clinical internship, internal institutional qualification, practice licensure, hearing aid fitting qualifications and medical device business requirements, and prescription and referral authority are different statuses: a degree does not automatically bring practice licensure, and fitting experience does not equal diagnostic and prescription authority. In Mainland China, hearing aid fitting follows the National Occupational Skill Standard for Hearing Aid Fitters (2020 edition) (Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security General Office Document No. 51 of 2020, occupation code 4-14-03-01, in four levels), and hearing aids are medical devices whose sale and use must also comply with medical device regulation requirements.

Occupation definition

The U.S. side is O*NET 29-1181.00 (Audiologists), and practice usually requires a state license; Mainland China has no practice license corresponding one-to-one to the U.S. "audiologist plus state license", and related positions are distributed across hospital ear, nose, and throat departments and hearing centers, rehabilitation institutions, hearing aid fitting organizations, and the special education system, and must be identified by employer nature and position sequence.
Education and major pathway

The United States usually requires a doctorate or professional degree such as the Au.D.; O*NET's education composition shows 95% doctorate and 5% postdoctoral training. Mainland China mainly trains people in audiology, hearing and speech rehabilitation, and assistive rehabilitation device technology, and specific standards are set by employers.
Practice licensure and fitting qualifications

U.S. states license audiologists, and the scope of the license and continuing education requirements are set by each state; in Mainland China hearing aid fitting is assessed by level under the National Occupational Skill Standard for Hearing Aid Fitters (2020 edition), and the skill level threshold for pediatric fitting is higher (the expert interpretation of that standard notes Level Three for ages 6—17 and Level Two for ages 0—6). Before starting, verify the scope of the license and qualifications, which cannot be inferred directly from a degree or an adjacent position.
Patient safety and infection control

The work involves ear canal examination and instrument contact, and cleaning, disinfection, and infection control must be carried out according to institutional systems; 43% are exposed to disease or infection sources every day. Operations involving patient health and safety should be carried out by personnel with the qualifications and protective conditions according to procedure.
Practice settings and scheduling

Practice settings include physicians' offices, hearing clinics, hospitals, schools, and private fitting organizations, and some positions require travel between locations; when comparing positions, write the patient volume, appointment and scheduling structure, and whether school audiology services are included into the written terms.
Continuing education and review

Equipment and devices are updated fairly quickly (O*NET lists 6 software skills and marks hot technologies, of which Microsoft Excel is marked as an in-demand skill), and practice licensure usually also requires continuing education; before starting, confirm the continuing education arrangements, case review, and skill update mechanisms.

entries.answer: They take the history related to hearing and balance and examine the ear canal and eardrum, perform pure-tone audiometry, speech audiometry, acoustic immittance, and auditory evoked potentials according to protocol, interpret the results, and form differential points; they then select and fit hearing aids, participate in cochlear implant programming, provide auditory training and communication strategy guidance, confirm outcomes through verification methods, and arrange follow-up; they also maintain medical records at each stage of the visit, provide advice to physicians, teachers, and employers, and participate in hearing screening and hearing conservation programs. subject.name: Audiologists
subject.summary: Audiologists assess and treat patients with hearing and related disorders, may fit hearing aids and provide auditory training, and may also conduct hearing-related research. On the U.S. side this corresponds to O*NET 29-1181.00 (Audiologists), in Job Zone Five (SVP 8.0 and above), with education mainly a doctorate or professional degree, and states usually require licensure to practice; Mainland China statistics are aggregated by industry category, do not list this occupation separately, and do not cover performance bonuses, fitting commissions, or project funding.
